seo.title: Best Street Food in Amman (2026) | tabiji.ai
seo.metaDescription: Discover Amman's top 12 street food spots for authentic falafel, shawarma, knafeh, and more. Your guide to delicious and affordable eats in Jordan's capital.

hero.subtitle: From bustling downtown stalls to modern takes on classics, Amman's street food scene is a vibrant tapestry of flavors, offering delicious and affordable bites that capture the city's culinary soul.

picks.name: Hashem Restaurant Downtown
picks.whyItMadeTheList: An Amman institution for over 90 years, Hashem offers a no-frills, authentic experience. It's famous for its delicious falafel, creamy fuul (fava beans), and humble atmosphere where locals and tourists alike gather on plastic chairs to enjoy simple yet perfect Middle Eastern breakfast and lunch staples.
picks.whatToOrder: Falafel platter, Hummus, Fuul, and a glass of mint tea.
picks.insiderTip: Go during off-peak hours (mid-morning or mid-afternoon) to avoid the biggest crowds, but embracing the bustle is part of the charm! Don't expect a menu; just point to what you want.
picks.redditQuote: "Seriously, you haven't done Amman until you've had a meal at Hashem Restaurant Downtown. The falafel is life-changing, and the whole vibe is just iconic."
picks.mapQuery: Hashem Restaurant, King Faisal Street, Downtown Amman, Jordan

picks.name: Shawarma Reem
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A legendary shawarma spot operating since 1978, Shawarma Reem is famed for its succulent lamb (or chicken) shawarma, thinly sliced and perfectly spiced. The limited menu ensures quality, focusing solely on perfecting their signature dish in a simple, takeaway-focused setting that often has a line out the door.
picks.whatToOrder: Lamb Shawarma sandwich. Don't ask for extras, just enjoy the classic!
picks.insiderTip: There's often a line, but it moves quickly. Grab your sandwich and find a spot nearby to enjoy it fresh. Parking can be tricky, so consider a taxi or walking.
picks.redditQuote: "Every time I'm in Amman, my first stop is Shawarma Reem. That lamb shawarma is just pure magic, melts in your mouth every single time."
picks.mapQuery: Shawarma Reem, Al Kulliyah Al Elmiyah Al Eslamiyah St, Amman, Jordan

picks.name: Habibah Sweets (Downtown)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Habibah is synonymous with knafeh in Amman. This iconic sweet shop, established in 1951, serves up hot, gooey, cheese-filled knafeh in a bustling stand-up setting. It's a must-visit for anyone with a sweet tooth, offering a truly authentic taste of Jordanian dessert culture that's loved by all generations.
picks.insiderTip: Be prepared to stand and eat; there's usually no seating. It's incredibly popular, so don't be surprised by a short wait, especially in the evenings.
picks.redditQuote: "If you leave Amman without trying knafeh from Habibah Sweets, you've made a terrible mistake. It's warm, cheesy, syrupy perfection, literally the best."
picks.mapQuery: Habibah Sweets Downtown, K. Hussein St., Amman, Jordan

picks.name: Al Quds Falafel
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Tucked away on Rainbow Street, Al Quds Falafel is a local favorite known for its consistently crispy falafel sandwiches, served in fresh bread with generous fillings of salad and tahini. It's a small, unpretentious spot perfect for a quick, delicious, and budget-friendly meal while exploring one of Amman's most vibrant streets.
picks.whatToOrder: Falafel sandwich with all the fixings.
picks.insiderTip: Grab a sandwich and take a stroll down Rainbow Street, enjoying the views and atmosphere. It's vegetarian-friendly and great for a quick snack.
picks.redditQuote: "After a walk on Rainbow Street, nothing beats a falafel sandwich from Al Quds Falafel. Simple, cheap, and so incredibly good."
picks.mapQuery: Al Quds Falafel, Rainbow Street, Jabal Amman, Jordan

picks.name: Abu Jbara
picks.whyItMadeTheList: While Hashem is famous downtown, Abu Jbara has established itself as a go-to for quality falafel and breakfast staples across Amman's more modern neighborhoods. Known for its fresh ingredients and clean, family-friendly atmosphere, it offers a slightly more comfortable sit-down experience than some of the older downtown spots, without sacrificing authenticity.
picks.whatToOrder: Hummus with minced meat (Hummus bi Lahme), crispy falafel, and a fresh salad.
picks.insiderTip: Great for breakfast or a hearty lunch. They also offer takeaway, which is convenient if you're on the go.
picks.redditQuote: "People rave about Hashem, but Abu Jbara is my personal favorite for consistently amazing hummus and falafel, especially their Khalda branch."
picks.mapQuery: Abu Jbara Restaurant, Al-Madina Al-Monawara St, Khalda, Amman, Jordan

picks.name: Sandwichat El-Maestro
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A bustling local spot specializing in delicious grilled sandwiches and skewers. El-Maestro is famous for its grilled chicken, liver, and meat sandwiches, prepared fresh on the spot with flavorful marinades and served in soft Arabic bread. It's a vibrant, lively place where you can watch your food being cooked.
picks.whatToOrder: Chicken liver sandwich (Kibdeh sandwich) or Shish Tawook sandwich.
picks.insiderTip: This place gets very busy, especially in the evenings. It's more of a stand-and-eat or grab-and-go experience.
picks.redditQuote: "The grilled liver sandwich from Sandwichat El-Maestro is my guilty pleasure in Amman. So rich and savory, perfect late-night grub."
picks.mapQuery: Sandwichat El-Maestro, Al Ba'ouniyah Street, Jebel Al Weibdeh, Amman, Jordan

picks.name: Fakher Bakery
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Fakher Bakery is a popular chain across Amman, renowned for its fresh mana'eesh – savory flatbreads baked in a stone oven with various toppings. From classic za'atar and cheese to more elaborate options, it's a staple for breakfast or a quick snack, offering a consistent and high-quality taste of this beloved Levantine treat.
picks.whatToOrder: Mana'eesh Za'atar (thyme and olive oil) and Mana'eesh Jibneh (cheese).
picks.insiderTip: Mana'eesh is best enjoyed hot and fresh from the oven. Pair it with a cup of tea or fresh juice for a perfect start to your day.
picks.redditQuote: "For a quick, delicious breakfast, you can't go wrong with Fakher Bakery. Their za'atar mana'eesh is just so satisfyingly fresh and flavorful."

picks.name: Mister Potato
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A modern take on street food, Mister Potato offers indulgent loaded fries with a variety of toppings, from melted cheese and sauces to chicken and jalapeños. It's a popular spot, especially among younger crowds, for a satisfying and customizable snack or meal that blends international fast-food trends with local flavor preferences.
picks.whatToOrder: The 'Amman Fries' with special sauce and crispy chicken, or build your own loaded potato.
picks.insiderTip: Great for a casual evening snack or if you're craving something different from traditional Arabic street food. Portions are generous.
picks.redditQuote: "After a night out, Mister Potato in Abdoun is my go-to for insane loaded fries. Their 'Amman Fries' combo is surprisingly good."
picks.mapQuery: Mister Potato, Abdoun Circle, Amman, Jordan

picks.name: Shawerma Al Dayaa
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Shawerma Al Dayaa offers a fantastic alternative to the more traditional shawarma spots, focusing on high-quality ingredients and a slightly cleaner, modern presentation. Their chicken shawarma, marinated with unique spices and often served with a special garlic sauce, has garnered a strong following for its rich flavor and consistent quality.
picks.whatToOrder: Chicken Shawarma (either in Lebanese bread or saj bread).
picks.insiderTip: They often have great combo deals. It's a good spot if you prefer a less crowded, more straightforward takeaway experience than some downtown options.
picks.redditQuote: "Forget the old classics, Shawerma Al Dayaa's chicken shawarma is seriously underrated. The garlic sauce is next level."
picks.mapQuery: Shawerma Al Dayaa, Prince Hashem Bin Al-Hussein St, Sweifieh, Amman, Jordan

picks.name: Falafel Al-Furat
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Falafel Al-Furat is another beloved spot known for its consistently fresh and crispy falafel, served hot and fast. Locals flock here for their satisfying falafel sandwiches and platters, often accompanied by fresh vegetables and pickles. It's a testament to Amman's strong falafel culture, offering reliable quality outside the immediate downtown area.
picks.whatToOrder: Falafel sandwich or a small falafel platter with hummus.
picks.insiderTip: Good for a quick breakfast or lunch on the go. The service is efficient, even when busy.
picks.redditQuote: "My favorite falafel outside of downtown is definitely Falafel Al-Furat on Gardens Street. Always fresh, always delicious."

picks.name: Al Kalha
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Al Kalha is a popular choice for traditional Jordanian breakfast and lunch, specializing in ful medames, hummus, and falafel. With multiple branches across the city, it offers a reliable and authentic taste of these staples, known for generous portions and a lively, local atmosphere that draws families and workers alike.
picks.whatToOrder: Fuul b’zeit (fava beans with olive oil) or Hummus bi tahini.
picks.insiderTip: Perfect for a hearty, authentic breakfast experience. Many locations have comfortable seating, unlike some downtown spots.
picks.redditQuote: "If you want a truly local experience for breakfast, Al Kalha has amazing fuul and hummus. It's less touristy than Hashem sometimes."
picks.mapQuery: Al Kalha Restaurant, Wasfi At-Tall St, Wahdat, Amman, Jordan

picks.name: Zalatimo Sweets
picks.whyItMadeTheList: While Habibah is famous for knafeh, Zalatimo Sweets has a long-standing reputation (since 1860) for a wider array of exquisite Arabic pastries, especially mutabbaq and baklava. Their dedication to traditional recipes and high-quality ingredients makes it a destination for those seeking a more varied sweet experience, offering delicate, rich, and perfectly balanced treats.
picks.whatToOrder: Mutabbaq (a thin pastry filled with cheese or nuts) or a selection of Baklava.
picks.insiderTip: Great for picking up gifts or trying a variety of sweets beyond knafeh. They usually have comfortable seating where you can enjoy your dessert with coffee.
picks.redditQuote: "Everyone goes for Habibah, but Zalatimo Sweets has the best mutabbaq, hands down. It's a different kind of sweet perfection."

faq.question: Is Amman street food safe to eat?
faq.answer: Yes, Amman street food is generally very safe to eat. Most establishments, especially the popular ones, have high turnover of fresh ingredients and operate with good hygiene standards. Stick to places that are busy with locals, as this is often a good indicator of freshness and quality. Always use your best judgment.

faq.question: What are the most popular street foods in Amman?
faq.answer: The most iconic street foods in Amman include falafel sandwiches (fried chickpea patties), shawarma (sliced roasted meat in bread), hummus and fuul (fava bean dip) for breakfast, and knafeh (a sweet cheese pastry) for dessert. Mana'eesh (savory flatbreads) are also a hugely popular quick bite.

faq.question: How much does street food cost in Amman?
faq.answer: Street food in Amman is very affordable. A filling falafel or shawarma sandwich typically costs between JOD 2-5 ($3-7 USD). A substantial breakfast of hummus and fuul might be JOD 3-7 ($4-9.5 USD) per person, and a piece of knafeh usually costs JOD 1-2 ($1.5-3 USD). You can eat very well on a budget.

faq.question: Are there vegetarian or vegan street food options in Amman?
faq.answer: Absolutely! Amman is very vegetarian and vegan-friendly when it comes to street food. Falafel, hummus, fuul, and mana'eesh (especially za'atar or vegetable-topped) are all plant-based and widely available. Just ensure to specify no dairy for mana'eesh if you are vegan.

faq.question: What's the best time of day to enjoy Amman's street food?
faq.answer: Amman's street food scene is vibrant all day long. Falafel, hummus, and mana'eesh are staples for breakfast and lunch. Shawarma is popular for lunch and dinner, often extending late into the night. Knafeh and other sweets can be enjoyed at any time, but are especially popular after meals or in the evening.

faq.question: Do street food vendors in Amman accept credit cards?
faq.answer: Most smaller, traditional street food vendors, especially those that are cash-only, will not accept credit cards. It is highly recommended to carry Jordanian Dinars (JOD) in small denominations when exploring the street food scene. Larger, more modern fast-food style street food spots might accept cards, but cash is king for authentic experiences.
